name: VSMC 300mm fab, Singapore

parties.note: Majority shareholder; contributes US$2.4 billion of equity for its 60% stake and is to run the fab.

parties.note: Minority shareholder; contributes US$1.6 billion of equity for its 40% stake; both partners also committed capacity deposits and are each allotted a share of the fab's capacity.

summary: The first 300 mm fab of VSMC, a specialty foundry joint venture of Vanguard International Semiconductor (60%) and NXP (40%) in Tampines, Singapore, announced in June 2024 at a cost of about US$7.8 billion, later reported as cut to US$6.7 billion. Ground was broken in December 2024, and the fab opened in September 2026 after about 22 months of construction, having entered risk production with first sample lots above 99% yield. VIS runs it, offering 130nm to 40nm processes for mixed-signal, power management, analog and interposer products. Volume production is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, with full capacity of about 44,000 wafers a month expected by 2029.

metrics.note: Total cost, funded by the partners' equity, US$1.9 billion of capacity deposits and usage fees, and third-party loans.
Reported reduction from US$7.8 billion, helped by equipment support from TSMC.
300 mm wafers per month expected in 2029, as stated at the groundbreaking.
300 mm wafers per month at full capacity by 2029; lowered from the 2024 figure after silicon interposer products were added.
Jobs the fab is expected to create, as stated at the opening.

milestones.note: VIS and NXP announced the joint venture, with technology expected to be licensed from TSMC.
More than 200 tools moved in and in use for trial production by May 2026.
Construction reported complete by the September 2026 opening.
Risk production under way, with the first sample lot processed, by September 2026.

notes: The fab is recorded as operating because it has opened and entered risk production with construction complete; volume production has not yet started. The partners said a second phase would be considered only after the first phase ramps; no second phase has been announced. The joint-venture terms come from trade press (s3) because the partners' own releases could not be read. VIS was also reported in May 2026 to be evaluating a second 12-inch fab without a decided location (s4); it is not part of this record.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Set the company to the joint venture's short partner names (VIS and NXP), removed an unsupported September 2024 formation date from the VIS party note, and dropped a 2029 date that the opening release does not attach to the 1,600 jobs. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): set the company to VIS, the 60% majority holder stated by TrendForce, added TSMC as the expected technology licensor (technology_partner), and recorded Tampines in the location note.
